utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-81-A, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to make sure, first, that the audio equipment is working properly. Mr. Perisic, can you hear me? I take it you can hear me, right? You cannot hear me? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I can hear now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Perisic. I will call now for the appearances of the parties. For the Prosecution, please. MS. MARTIN SALGADO: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Elena Martin Salgado, and I'm appearing on behalf of the Prosecution with Bronagh McKenna and Djurdja Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for Mr. Perisic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all the participants in the proceedings. My name is Novak Lukic, attorney-at-law at law from Belgrade, and I shall represent Mr. Perisic in this courtroom today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. As you are aware, Rule 65 ter (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal, and, thereafter, within 120 days after the last Status Conference for each Appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A Status Conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the Appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the Appellants with respect to the status of their case. The Status Conference is also an opportunity for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. In the present case, the last Status Conference was held on 7 March 2012. Today's Status Conference was scheduled by an order -- order issued on 18 June 2012. Let me therefore start the substantive part of this Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Perisic's health. Mr. Perisic, if you prefer this discussion to be held in closed session, please indicate and I will ... THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes. I would like to speak in closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: We are in open session, I take it, right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are now in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I turn to the update of the case. There is one confidential motion currently pending which will be decided in due course. And I would like, at this stage, ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise with me at this time. Let me start from the Prosecution. MS. MARTIN SALGADO: Thank you, Your Honour. We do not have any issues to raise at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no issues to raise either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Since there are no other matters that any of the parties would like to raise at this stage, it remains only for me to thank the parties for their attendance, thank the interpreters and the Registry staff, and I will call the proceedings to a close. We will now rise.
